subject: Kappa.ai deal — GPU footprint fit & ops playbook

Subject: Kappa.ai sizing kickoff — sample demand + ask

Hi Leah / Ethan,

Following up from last week's call — attaching our quick demand CSV (kappa_demand_estimates.csv) with the traffic shape you shared in the demo. To get a concrete Dedicated recommendation we need to lock a few inputs:

- Typical request size (median tokens) and 95th percentile tokens per request
- Target SLOs: p50/p95 latency targets for generate endpoints and any hard p99 limits
- Expected steady-state QPS and promotional burst profiles (hours/days)

Quick note on our framing: we size Dedicated capacity in GPU slabs sized to meet your target p95 SLO at baseline load, then add headroom for peak and a safety slab for model rollouts/maintenance. A short example: if median request is 60 tokens and steady QPS is 150, that's 9k tokens/sec of sustained output; we map that to per-GPU tokens/sec for the chosen model variant to get an initial GPU count, then add 30–100% headroom depending on burst risk and SLA.

Can you confirm median and p95 tokens per request and whether you need p95 < 750ms for the main generate endpoint? If you prefer, send a small sample of logs and we can backfill the estimates.

Thanks,

Thanks Ben — attaching the brief you asked for. Quick answers inline:

- Median tokens per request: 48
- 95th percentile tokens per request: 210
- Target SLOs: p50 ~ 150–200ms, p95 target 600ms for interactive flows; we can tolerate p99 up to 1.2s for non-critical background jobs.
- Steady QPS: 120 req/s; promotional burst profile: up to 400 req/s sustained for ~30 minutes, plus very short bursts to 1k req/s for <2 minutes during marketing sends.

We also want the ability to roll a new model variant without impacting the baseline (canary + fast fallback). Ideally we'd reserve capacity to absorb a failed canary and still meet p95.

Thanks — Leah

Subject: Re: Fwd: Kappa.ai sizing kickoff — sample demand + ask

Ben — quick capacity sketch and ops recommendations below. I kept numbers conservative; we can tighten with perf traces.

Assumptions used
- Model in production: rw-13b-quant (q4_0) for baseline; fallback: rw-7b-quant.
- Measured per-GPU sustained throughput (observed in our fleet):
  • rw-13b-quant-ish: ~3,500 tokens/sec sustained (single inference stream concurrency optimized)
  • rw-7b-quant-ish: ~6,500 tokens/sec sustained
- Median tokens per request: 48 → 120 tokens for p95 bucket (we use 120 to budget headroom vs p95 210 from their sample)
- Latency targets: translate p95<=600ms into max acceptable model compute time per request; we budget ~400ms compute + ~150ms networking/queuing for p95.

Sizing math (steady)
- Steady: 120 req/s * median 48 tokens = 5,760 tokens/sec sustained.
- Required GPUs (baseline, rw-13b): 5,760 / 3,500 ≈ 1.65 → round up to 2 GPUs.
- For p95 tail (accounting for larger requests): assume effective tokens/sec demand 120 req/s * 120 tokens = 14,400 tokens/sec.
  • GPUs needed to keep p95 compute headroom: 14,400 / 3,500 ≈ 4.1 → 5 GPUs to avoid queuing under heavy-tail.

Burst planning (promo)
- Promo sustained: 400 req/s * median 48 = 19,200 tokens/sec → 19,200 / 3,500 ≈ 5.5 → 6 GPUs.
- Short spikes to 1,000 req/s (very short, <2m): 1,000 * 48 = 48,000 tokens/sec → 48,000 / 3,500 ≈ 13.7 → ~14 GPUs. For very short spikes we recommend autoscaling into a burst pool (Dedicated burst capacity) rather than committing 14 GPUs permanently.

Headroom recommendation
- Baseline commit: 5 GPUs (covers p95 heavy-tail for steady traffic and gives room for canaries). This maps to expected p95 compute headroom with rw-13b quant variant.
- Promo buffer (reserved burst capacity): additional 6 GPUs reserved in burst pool that can be autoscaled in for sustained promos (gives you ability to handle 400 req/s).
- Short spike fallback: allow autoscale to tap cloud-burst (spot or partner pool) up to +9 GPUs (total peak ~14) for <5 mins; configure fast fallback to rw-7b-quant for degraded quality but lower latency if burst capacity delayed.
- Equivalent commit footprint if Kappa prefers a single committed slab: 11 GPUs (5 baseline + 6 promo buffer). Recommend 12 if they want a 1 GPU safety buffer.

Ops/runbook bullets
- Enable prefix (KV) caching for common prompts — reduces tokens sent to model for multi-turn.
- Configure continuous batching with max latency target 100ms to avoid queueing spikes affecting p95.
- Canary strategy: 10% traffic canary on separate slab; if canary fails, immediate traffic route to rw-7b-quant fallback slab (we recommend 2 rw-7b GPUs reserved to absorb fallback).
- Monitoring: surface p95 p99 and GPU util% per slab; set automation to pre-warm burst pool 2 minutes prior to known promos.

Estimate summary (conservative):
- Commit recommendation: 5 GPUs (rw-13b-quant)
- Promo reserved burst: +6 GPUs (on-demand burst pool)
- Short spike autoscale: up to +9 GPUs via cloud-burst (fast fallback to rw-7b if delayed)
- Ops: KV caching + continuous batching + canary slab (10%) + playbook (attached).

I'll attach the short playbook and a spreadsheet with the math (kappa_commit_summary.xlsx). If we want to optimize cost, we can rerun with tighter token p95 numbers from request traces — that often drops baseline GPUs down by 1.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Kappa.ai sizing kickoff — plan & next steps

Leah / Ethan — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Karthik's conservative sketch, here's the recommended proposal we will include in the SOW:

1) Committed Dedicated footprint: 5 x rw-13b-quant GPUs to meet p95 targets at steady-state (includes canary headroom).
2) Promo reserved burst: +6 GPUs available via reserved burst pool (pre-warm rules).
3) Short spike policy: autoscale up to +9 GPUs from partner cloud-burst for <5 minute events; fallback to rw-7b-quant (2 GPUs reserved) if autoscale lag occurs.
4) Ops playbook: we will deliver (a) KV-prefix caching enablement, (b) continuous batching tuning, (c) 10% canary slab & automatic fallback policy, and (d) runbook for pre-warm on marketing sends.

Next steps:
- I'll send a formal SOW/quote with these numbers and an optional cost-optimized variant (swap 1–2 rw-13b GPUs for rw-7b + more software caching) by EOD.
- Leah: please confirm whether Kappa wants the promo reserved as part of the commit (adds to monthly seat/commit) or prefer to pay for burst usage on-demand.
- We'll include the redwood_capacity_playbook.pdf and the kappa_commit_summary.xlsx with the proposal. DocuSign link will follow.

Ben Carter
